note: Single aerial view, 1536x1109, uploaded as own work by user 'Reply.rajrewal' (apparently Raj Rewal's office). Also File:Asian Games Village.jpg (751px, interior lanes, too small). Not in a building-specific category.

name: Australian Islamic Centre
note: No Commons files. Sources confirm a flat roof with rows of 3 m gold, three-sided (triangular) lanterns, but disagree on their number (96 vs 55) and say little about the walls, entry court and the large triangular side wall, so the elevation below the roof would be guessed.

name: Belapur Artists' Village
note: No Commons files. The cluster logic is well documented (7 houses round an 8 x 8 m court, then 12 x 12 m courts), but the idea is a plan and sources don't settle the house roofs (pitched tiles or flat) or heights, so an elevation would be guessed.

name: Bridge School
view: side elevation across the creek: the timber-slatted steel truss box (about 28 m long) resting on concrete supports on each bank, with the village footbridge hung underneath
note: No Commons files found. The two tulou at either end are left out to keep the drawing about the school itself. Box height is estimated (sources give only 28 m long x 8.5 m wide).

name: Capuchinas Chapel
note: No Commons files. Everything that defines it (yellow light, lattice cross, the 'keel' wall) is inside; the street exterior is plain and undocumented in the sources reached. An interior drawing would need reliable plans/photos.

name: Casa Bianchi
commons_category: Category:Bianchi House (Via Formeggie 6, Riva San Vitale)
view: side elevation: the square concrete-block tower on the slope above Lake Lugano, with the steel Warren-truss footbridge running from the hillside road straight into the top floor
note: Commons has only one photo (File:Κατοικία Μπιάντσι (Bianchi House).jpg, 736px, too small). The 'Casa Bianchi, Ligornetto' panoramio photos are a different Botta house. Sources disagree on 4 or 5 levels; the drawing keeps the facade openings simple (one deep upper opening where the bridge arrives, one vertical slit below) rather than reproducing every cut-out.

name: Farming Kindergarten
note: No Commons files. The idea is clear (one continuous looping green-roof strip round three courtyards, rising to two storeys), but the exact loop geometry and where it rises and falls can't be confirmed without plans, and the form only reads in a bird's-eye view.

name: Fuji Kindergarten
view: bird's-eye oblique view of the single-storey oval ring: the flat roof deck around the open courtyard, with the low glazed outer wall in front
note: No Commons files found (the 'Fuji Kindergarten' files on Commons are other kindergartens in Hokkaido). Proportions follow the sources: about 183 m round the outside, 108 m round the courtyard, 2.1 m ceilings. The zelkova trees that grow through the roof are left out because the drawing rules forbid trees, and roof railings are left out for simplicity.

name: Grand National Assembly Mosque
note: No Commons files found. Sources confirm a low building with a stepped pyramidal roof, a glass qibla wall and a triangular forecourt, mostly sunk into the slope, but not the number of roof steps, the proportions or the minaret, so the drawing would be guessed.

name: Green School Bali
note: No Commons files (an en.wikipedia article 'Green School (Bali)' exists with no images). The main 'Heart of School' is a complex spiralling bamboo structure; its form can't be established from the text sources reachable from here.

name: Hikma Religious and Secular Complex
note: No Commons files. Sources describe the programme (old mud-brick mosque turned library, new compressed-earth mosque, minaret, courts) but not the massing, heights or openings.

name: Liyuan Library
note: No Commons files. One source gives a 30 x 4.35 x 6.3 m box clad in about 45,000 sticks with roof glazing, but no source confirms the roof shape or how the sticks are laid, and the stick skin is the whole point of the building. Close to drawable if the owner can confirm from a photo.
